name: Hashabiah
overview: Hashabiah was a male Levite known as the son of Mattaniah according to Nehemiah 11:22. His identification as a Levite situates him within the tribe set apart for priestly and temple duties. Beyond his lineage, Scripture provides no additional details about his life or role.
namesAndTitles: The name Hashabiah means 'YHWH has reckoned,' reflecting a theologically rich meaning connected to the divine name YHWH. This proper name, recorded in Nehemiah 11:22, does not appear to have been given directly by God but carries a significant spiritual connotation.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly records Hashabiah as the son of Mattaniah and, by inference, the grandson of Bani as noted in Nehemiah 11:22. No further familial relationships are documented beyond these.
scriptureSignificance: Hashabiah's mention in Nehemiah 11:22 places him among the Levites who were resettled in Jerusalem during the post-exilic period, underscoring his role in the restoration of temple worship and community life. His lineage highlights the continuity of the Levitical priestly heritage essential for maintaining covenant faithfulness. Though brief, his record affirms the faithfulness of God's people in preserving the priestly line through generations.
